itemText: The API starts in production without an email provider key
The auth secret is required in production and must be long enough
The owner email is read from one setting and the deploy workflow sets it from a GitHub variable
The env tests describe the new rules
Add an owner email setting to the API environment schema and validate it as an email.
Require the auth secret (minimum length) in production whether or not an email key exists; keep the email-only settings required only when an email key exists.
Update the environment tests that asserted the secret was only needed with an email key.
Pass the owner email variable to the API service in the deploy workflow; leave existing secret lines untouched.
[blocked: user] Confirm the owner email is a GitHub variable (recommended, not secret) named for production, not a secret.
Ensuring the owner twice creates one user
Email comparison ignores case and spaces
Anyone else is never the owner
Add a module that reads the configured owner email, checks a submitted email against it, and ensures the owner row exists using the existing idempotent create.
Add tests for repeat calls, case differences and a different email.
Make the existing create-user helper reusable by the module without changing its behaviour.
Sign-up is disabled and any non-owner email gets the generic failure
Passwords shorter than 12 characters are rejected
Sign-in attempts are limited per client IP in the database store
Email and password sign-in also returns a session token for native callers
The API starts and signs in with no email provider key
Turn on built-in email and password with sign-up disabled, minimum length 12 and no email verification step.
Add the bundled bearer plugin from the installed Better Auth so sessions can be sent as a token.
Add a before-sign-in rule that rejects any email other than the owner with the same error as a wrong password.
Add custom rate-limit rules for the key, password and sign-out paths (5 per minute per IP for sign-in).
Extend the integration test to cover owner-only, sign-up refusal, rate limiting and token return.
Register magic link only when an email key exists, and register the key sign-in plugin.
Add a Better Auth plugin with a POST key sign-in endpoint taking the key in the body only.
Reuse the existing hash and active-token lookup; reject tokens linked to a different user; compare hashes with a constant-time compare.
Ensure the owner exists, create the session and set the cookie using Better Auth's own session helpers.
Return one fixed error body for every failure and make sure no log call receives the key.
Add tests for each criterion, including a log-capture test and a revoked key.
A valid active key returns a session cookie for the owner and creates the owner on first use
Unknown, revoked, malformed, empty and other-user keys all give the same response
The comparison of key hashes is constant time and last use is recorded
Neither the key nor its hash appears in logs or error output
Foreign origin is refused
Add a credential classifier and a third accepted credential (session token) to the gate after the two existing ones.
Let the three native auth paths bypass the shared-secret-only rule and the up-front gate, still rate limited and origin checked.
Rewrite the session status check to use secret plus owner email; remove the user count and its caching.
Update the status tests that expected unconfigured for no email key and for no user, and remove the user-count caching tests.
Update the route tests for the gate, add tests for the carve-out and for old credentials still passing.
Shared secret and device tokens behave exactly as before on every route
A valid session token is accepted; expired, revoked or tampered ones are refused
Only email and password sign-in, sign-out and session lookup are reachable without the shared secret; key sign-in and the rest of the auth paths still need it
Status is unconfigured only when the auth secret or owner email is missing
A missing user row no longer means unconfigured
Add a set-owner-password script using Better Auth's own hashing, a hidden prompt and the minimum-length rule.
Add a revoke-key script by label or id that revokes and clears sessions.
Add package scripts for both next to the existing create-user script.
Add tests for the pure parts: password validation and revoke selection.
[blocked: user] Hidden prompt without a new dependency (recommended: Node's built-in terminal input with echo off) or add a prompt library.
The password is read with hidden typing, twice, and never passed as an argument or printed
Setting the password again replaces it and ends all owner sessions
Revoking a key marks it revoked and ends all owner sessions
Scripts refuse to run against a non-local database unless the owner passes an explicit confirmation flag
Key and password forms each show one generic failure and a separate too-many-attempts message
The key field is a password-type input that is not remembered or logged
The email-link option shows only when available
Successful sign-in lands on the home page; sign-out unchanged
Add key sign-in and password sign-in calls and outcome types to the browser helpers.
Allow both new endpoints in the web proxy allowlist with POST only.
Rebuild the login form with a method choice, the two forms and the optional link form.
Learn availability of the email link from a non-secret setting or the status result without a new secret.
Update the proxy, browser and form tests and add tests for each outcome message.
A new web auth doc exists with methods, sessions, rate limits and rotation steps
The mobile auth doc mentions the session-token path next to the device token
Local setup docs explain minting a key and setting the password
Create the web auth architecture doc in present tense with the credential order and rotation table.
Update the mobile study app auth section and the iOS readme (sign-in marked planned).
Update local dev docs for the new scripts.
[blocked: user] Confirm the production shared secret exists, then require it at API start-up.
